title: Linux VFS (Virtual File System)
summary: The VFS (Virtual File System) is the abstraction layer for filesystems in Linux. Key structures: superblock (filesystem metadata), inode (file metadata), dentry (directory entry, name-to-inode mapping), file (open file description). Operations: super_operations (alloc_inode, destroy_inode, read_inode, write_inode, put_super, statfs), inode_operations (lookup, create, link, unlink, symlink, mkdir, rmdir, rename, permission, getattr, setattr), file_operations (read, write, open, release, llseek, ioctl, mmap, poll, fsync, fasync, lock, splice_read, splice_write).

structure.meaning: Filesystem-level metadata: magic, block size, root inode, operations, list of inodes, etc.
File metadata: mode, uid, gid, size, timestamps, block pointers, operations. Identified by inode number.
Directory entry: name, parent, inode, hash, children list. Cached in dentry cache (dcache).
Open file description: file position (f_pos), flags, mode, dentry, operations, private data.
alloc_inode, destroy_inode, read_inode, write_inode, drop_inode, put_super, write_super, statfs, remount_fs, etc.
lookup, create, link, unlink, symlink, mkdir, rmdir, mknod, rename, permission, getattr, setattr, etc.
llseek, read, write, read_iter, write_iter, iopoll, poll, unlocked_ioctl, compat_ioctl, mmap, open, flush, release, fsync, fasync, lock, splice_read, splice_write, etc.
readpage, writepage, writepages, set_page_dirty, readpages, write_begin, write_end, bmap, invalidatepage, releasepage, etc.

notes: VFS allows multiple filesystems (ext4, XFS, FAT, tmpfs, proc, sysfs) to coexist.
The dentry cache (dcache) caches name-to-inode lookups for performance.
The page cache (address_space) caches file data in memory.
VFS operations are dispatched via function pointers (polymorphism in C).
Every filesystem implements the VFS interface (super_operations, inode_operations, file_operations).
